article_title: DuckDB Benchmarks Its v2.0 Preview on NVIDIA Vera, Reporting a 46% TPC-H SF1,000 Edge Over an Intel Xeon 6 Baseline

content_preview.title: DuckDB Benchmarks Its v2.0 Preview on NVIDIA Vera, Reporting a 46% TPC-H SF1,000 Edge Over an Intel Xeon 6 Baseline
content_preview.summary: DuckDB's team ran a v2.0 development build on NVIDIA's Vera CPU and an Intel Xeon 6 server, reporting median TPC-H SF1,000 scores of 3,073,292.99 versus 2,109,782.19 QphH@Size.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The DuckDB team published a benchmark of a development build of DuckDB v2.0 running on NVIDIA's Vera CPU on October 16, 2026. According to the [DuckDB blog](https://duckdb.org/2026/10/16/nvidia-vera-benchmark.html), written by Gábor Szárnyas, the Vera platform showed "a 46% performance advantage on TPC-H SF1,000 over the x86 baseline (Intel Xeon 6)." The post says the work was done in collaboration with the NVIDIA team, and it frames the numbers as the team's own runs rather than au...

editor_notes.content_quality: Compact, well-structured Briefing (573 words, within the 300-800 range). Covers setup, per-platform configuration, a full run table and explicit limitations. Internal cross-reference /article/2026-09/30-duckdb-156-... resolves to an existing published article (singular /article/ form).
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three snapshots (source-0, source-1, source-2 .html.gz, all HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null for all) as extracted plain text, and re-fetched the two numeric-critical pages live as raw HTML via curl (not a summarizer); live and snapshot agree. source-0 (duckdb.org/2026/10/16/nvidia-vera-benchmark.html, Gabor Szarnyas, 2026-10-16): confirms the medians 3,073,292.99 (Vera) and 2,109,782.19 (x86), all six per-run scores in the article table exactly (x86 2,120,588.82 / 2,022,795.01 / 2,109,782.19; Vera 3,073,292.99 / 3,131,306.27 / 3,052,102.87), SF1,000, 'full TPC-H benchmark (not just the read queries!)', warmup run discarded then three complete runs with median of QphH@Size, Ubuntu 26.04, 768 GB memory, single NVMe SSD 3+ TB ext4, preview build 1.6.0.dev379 with the duckdb-tpch harness, block_allocator_memory '500G', allocator_background_threads true, Xeon 6 with 96 cores / 192 threads run at 96 threads, Vera 88 cores with Spatial Multithreading on a dual-socket system restricted to one socket via numactl, threads=88, arm64 regular build, up to 1.2 TB/s memory bandwidth, 'in collaboration with the NVIDIA team', the three attributed factors, and the closing sentence about v2.0.0 stable / full dual-socket. The quoted '46% performance advantage on TPC-H SF1,000 over the x86 baseline (Intel Xeon 6)' and the 'top 3' quote are verbatim substrings. The post says 88 'Olympus' cores itself, so the claim is supported by the DuckDB post independently of NVIDIA. source-1 (nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/vera-cpu/): raw text contains 'NVIDIA Vera features 88 custom Olympus cores ... Spatial Multithreading creates 176 threads' (live curl also returned '88 custom Olympus cores'); article's phrase is accurate. source-2 (duckdb.org/2026/09/28/announcing-duckdb-156.html): 'Looking Ahead: DuckDB v2.0 on Windows', Windows 11, TPC-H SF300, v1.5.6 total 822 s vs v2.0.0-dev 129 s, matches the article. Allowlist: nvidia.com (line 397) and duckdb.org (line 2399) both already present by exact hostname; no allowlist edit needed. Orphan-link diff: body URLs equal article.sources exactly (empty diff both directions).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: 46% check: 3,073,292.99 / 2,109,782.19 - 1 = 45.67%, rounds to 46%; the article presents 46% as the DuckDB post's own stated figure (quoted and attributed), which is correct and matches the computation. Median, SF1,000, hardware configuration and single-socket restriction are all accurate. TPC-H compliance wording: the article never calls the numbers 'TPC-H results' or official; it describes 'TPC-H SF1,000 scores', says 'unaudited results' and reports the post's conditional 'if audited ... would stand a chance to be in the top 3' as a conditional. Note the post itself does not use the word 'unaudited'; the article's characterisation is the editor-supported inference from 'if we were to audit these results', which is accurate. 'Does not report price or power comparison' and 'no v2.0 release date in the post' are both true of the post. Minor: the article says the Xeon 6 is a 'baseline'; the post does not name the exact SKU and the article does not claim one.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. Numbers are attributed to DuckDB; the performance explanation is presented as 'the team attributes'. No promotional language or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: New story. Related coverage is the DuckDB 1.5.6 article (referenced and linked) and the DuckDB agent-mode article; no overlap with the Vera benchmark. No other article reports this benchmark.
concerns: Independence/conflict: the benchmark is vendor-collaborated (DuckDB states it was done 'in collaboration with the NVIDIA team', NVIDIA supplied the Vera hardware) and is self-run and unaudited; the only corroborating source (nvidia.com) is itself a vendor page, and no independent third-party replication is cited. The article discloses the collaboration and the unaudited status in the Overview and in 'What We Don't Know'; editor judges this disclosure adequate for a Briefing.

The x86 and Vera systems differ in more than the CPU (core counts, memory type per NVIDIA page is LPDDR5X vs DDR5, thread settings); the post does not provide system-level details beyond those reported, and the article does not generalize beyond them.
recommendations: Future coverage should seek an independent replication or the audited TPC-H result if one is filed after DuckDB v2.0.0 stable ships.
Consider stating the 45.7% unrounded figure alongside the post's 46% when a derived figure is relevant.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed Briefing. Every number, quote, configuration detail and date traces to the cited sources; vendor collaboration and unaudited status are disclosed. No corrections required. APPROVE. The scanner's findings list was empty and suspicious_patterns were null for all sources.
